deltas.delta: Base v1.6.0-rc.1 is tagged. It moves Base from revm 42.0.1 and revm-interpreter 42.0.0 to revm 43.0.3, revm-interpreter 43.0.2 and revm-context 43.0.3, keeps ruint 1.19.0, and moves reth-evm to base/reth rev 2b20e42 (2.8.1). deltas.delta: Everest (Base Transactions, EIP-8430) is still TBD on Sepolia and mainnet. Since Cobalt, Base nodes read upgrade timestamps from a contract on Ethereum, so a fork date can be set without a client release (metrics-only on mainnet today). The v1.6.0-rc.1 phase loop runs each phase under a revm journal checkpoint and reverts it on failure; revm-context 43.0.3 reverts TransientStorageChange entries in checkpoint_revert.

Base v1.5.6, the running build, clears transient storage after every transaction: its handler calls commit_tx after execution and, for a failed deposit, checkpoint_revert to the first checkpoint then commit_tx, and discard_tx otherwise (crates/common/evm/src/handler.rs:340-386); revm-context 42.0.0, which v1.5.6 pins, clears transient_storage in commit_tx and discard_tx (src/journal/inner.rs:141-192). World Chain uses the stock op-revm handler.

cleared.check: Battery (99,985 vectors) and targeted set (85,544 vectors) at the builds that answer on 2026-11-25, which the cycle 21 critic named as untested: MULMOD, ADDMOD, DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, SIGNEXTEND, SAR, SHL, SHR, BYTE, EXP, comparisons, JUMPI conditions, KECCAK256, MCOPY overlaps, CALLDATALOAD past the end and the FullMath 512 bit product.
cleared.result: All 185,529 vectors return the specified word on all seven chains, with no error. The pool math that depends on these opcodes (FullMath mulmod at src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24,48,112, SqrtPriceMath.sol:252, TickMath sign handling at src/libraries/TickMath.sol:61-63, tick compression at src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:20-26,54-67, BitMath byte lookup at src/libraries/BitMath.sol:17-22) therefore computes as on Ethereum at these builds.

cleared.check: Script sets 1 (250 scripts, 12,322 calls of pool math, settlement and claims) and 2 (300 scripts, 16,263 calls through hook, token and native payout paths) on the deployed PoolManager bytecode at today's builds.
cleared.result: All 250 and all 300 scripts give the same bytes as the Ethereum reference on every one of the seven chains, including the 1,264 failing calls with eleven revert selectors. OP Mainnet's endpoint served two builds during the run, so the result covers whichever answered; cycle 19 pinned both.

cleared.check: Mined swaps since the earlier windows: tick relation, single-step formulas and full Pool.swap replay from parent-block state (swaps.py, replay.py).
cleared.result: 16,427 swaps read on the seven chains all satisfy the tick relation (13 on a lower tick boundary, as src/libraries/Pool.sol leaves after a swap that ends on a tick going down). All 94 multi-step and crossed-liquidity swaps sampled, the longest with 12 steps on Zora, replay to the unit. Block production on these chains computed the same pool math as the source.

cleared.check: op-reth v2.10.0, the final release after the rc.4 build three of these chains run in production: integer library, interpreter and op-revm changes.
cleared.result: No change on the PoolManager's path. revm 43.0.3, revm-interpreter 43.0.2 and ruint 1.20.0 are pinned as in rc.4, and the op-revm source files read are byte identical. The instruction table is the stock mainnet table.

cleared.check: Base v1.6.0-rc.1 links the evm2 interpreter (alloy-rs/evm2 rev 9b037449), an interpreter no earlier cycle read at this revision, while keeping ruint 1.19.0 whose narrow shift fast paths are known faulty for amounts of 2^32 and above.
cleared.result: evm2 does not execute on Base at this release. base-common-evm2 states that it is not wired into the node, and no crate in the v1.6.0-rc.1 lockfile depends on it, so blocks and eth_call still run revm-interpreter 43.0.2, whose SHL, SHR and SAR handlers clamp the shift amount before calling ruint (cycle 21 reading). The rc.1 also moves Base to the revm 43 line that op-reth already runs and that the seven-chain rerun covers.

cleared.check: World Chain's own EVM crate (world-chain-evm in v2.8.2 and v2.8.3): does it replace an instruction, add a precompile or execute in parallel.
cleared.result: No. It wraps OpEvmConfig over OpEvmFactory with the stock op-revm instruction table and precompiles, adds a witness cache and collector that record finished state, and forwards Lagoon post-execution hooks to op-reth's. Execution of each transaction is the op-revm path that the battery covers.

cleared.check: Which block producers run a code path other than the public endpoint: external builders behind rollup-boost (op-rbuilder and World Chain's PBH builder).
cleared.result: A builder's block reaches the chain only after the sequencer's own execution client and every follower execute it again; rollup-boost validates the builder payload with engine_newPayload on the local client and falls back to the local block, and the canonical chain is derived from L1 batches that verifiers re-execute. A builder that computed a pool result differently would produce a block that the clients answering these RPCs reject. The validation call in rollup-boost's server.rs discards the returned status and acts only on a transport error (lines 277-281 of the published source), so an invalid builder block surfaces at op-node's own newPayload instead; that is liveness at operator level and moves no funds. The rollup-boost text was read through search highlights of the published pages.

cleared.check: Pointer width of the proof programs that settle withdrawals (premise of lead L-964): kona-client 1.9.0 on Cannon and Base's SP1 range program.
cleared.result: Both are 64 bit targets. kona-client is built for mips64-unknown-none with target-pointer-width 64 and the corrected target-c-int-width 32 at tag kona-client/v1.9.0 (the c-int-width 64 error of the old builder image, which made str comparisons fail, is fixed in that file). SP1 builds for riscv64im-succinct-zkvm-elf with the lp64 ABI. usize is 64 bits on both, so the 32 bit branches of ruint and of revm's saturating conversions are not compiled into either program.

cleared.check: Critic gap of cycle 21 for L-101 on the builds that have their own handler: does a failed or halted deposit, or any transaction, leave transient storage for the next transaction on Base v1.5.6 and World Chain.
cleared.result: No. Base v1.5.6 commits through commit_tx after execution, reverts a failed deposit to the first checkpoint and commits, and calls discard_tx on other errors (crates/common/evm/src/handler.rs:340-386); revm-context 42.0.0 clears transient_storage in commit_tx and discard_tx (src/journal/inner.rs:141-192). World Chain uses op-revm's stock handler through OpEvmFactory. The lock flag, deltas and synced reserves of src/libraries/Lock.sol:13-25 and CurrencyReserves.sol:17-36 therefore cannot outlive a transaction. Zora's conduit-op-reth source is not public and was not read.

cleared.check: Base Transactions phase loop in the first tagged release that carries it (v1.6.0-rc.1, eip8130.rs execute_calls): can a failed phase keep TSTORE writes while its storage writes and transfers are undone (lead L-891).
cleared.result: No. Each phase takes a journal checkpoint before its first call (eip8130.rs:1394), a failed or policy-blocked call marks the phase reverted, checkpoint_revert undoes it and every later phase is skipped (lines 1458-1474), and a completed phase is merged with checkpoint_commit (line 1483). In revm-context 43.0.3, which rc.1 pins, checkpoint_revert drains the journal and reverts every entry with the transient map passed in (src/journal/inner.rs:622-640), and a TransientStorageChange entry restores the old value (revm-context-interface 43.0.2 src/journaled_state/entry.rs:454-468), so a sync recorded at src/PoolManager.sol:279-288 inside a failed phase is rolled back with it.

cleared.check: Upcoming forks for six months: Lagoon on the six Superchain members and Everest on Base. What changes for the PoolManager's arithmetic and logic the day after.
cleared.result: Nothing on the opcode path. Lagoon is not scheduled and keeps the Osaka instruction set; its precompile change is to BLS12-381, which the PoolManager does not call. Its post-execution transaction and SuperchainETHBridge were cleared in cycle 19, and its predeploys are not yet installed anywhere (lead L-892 stays open). Everest has no date; its phase loop restores transient storage as read in v1.6.0-rc.1. No other upgrade is announced for these chains.

The premise does not hold for the programs in use. Both proof programs are 64 bit: kona-client 1.9.0 targets mips64-unknown-none with target-pointer-width 64, and SP1 programs target riscv64im with the lp64 ABI. usize is 64 bits on both, so the 32 bit branches of ruint 1.18.0 to 1.20.0 and of revm's saturating conversions are not compiled into either; the 64 bit branches are the ones cycle 21 tested on x86_64. Architecture-specific code generation stays with F-126, F-131 and L-694.

Base still runs base/v1.5.6 (census today), so the v1.5.6 readings apply. An account with no role can call transfer, transferWithMemo and approve on a B20 token and nothing that writes another holder's balance (cycle 6 trials of 30 functions, cycle 7 reading of every balance and allowance write: move_balance from transfer with the caller as source, transferFrom after the allowance check, seize with the Seize role, burn and mint with roles). transfer credits exactly the named recipient and only rejects zero and the token itself (cycle 16, credit_recipient.rs), so a transfer cannot return true while the tokens go elsewhere. The factory's privileged path runs only for a token created in the same call, a policy update needs the policy admin (F-107 shows the Unauthorized revert), and a token can only bind an existing policy. The issuer and list admin powers remain F-027 and F-107. A reread at the next Base release is opened as a new lead.
